focus: REDO key question 10 with a full inbound-reference enumeration across references/ and assets/ in all four hubs, then key question 11 UX by running two sk-doc validators on deliberately broken copies under /tmp and quoting the operator-visible error text
answeredQuestions: Which templates, references, assets or modes across the four hubs have no inbound route or duplicate another, and what breaks if each is removed?

label: palette-sheet-ordered.html and palette-sheet-categorical.html under sk-design-chart/assets/style-reference/evilcharts have no consumer anywhere: the only non-manifest mention of either is its own self-declaration meta tag, while the documented skeleton palette-sheet-neutral.html is cited three times in template-contract.md, three times in scripts/README.md and three times in the colour-comes-from-one-source playbook. Nothing named in a script, reference, playbook or test breaks if the two siblings are removed. Caveat: apply-design-md.test.cjs reads assets/style-reference as a directory, so a directory-enumerating assertion could notice the removal; that test was not executed.

evilcharts/source-globals.css is provenance-only: its own header comment is the only text describing it and no DESIGN.md, reference or script opens it. Removing it costs the raw captured upstream source behind the Style Reference derivation but breaks nothing functional, because DESIGN.md explains the design language in prose independently.

validate_skill_package.py surfaces exactly one frontmatter error per run because it shells out to package_skill.py --check and prints only that subprocess's Output tail, which aborts on the first missing field. A probe missing name, description and allowed-tools needed three separate validator runs, each reporting only the next field, so every incomplete skill costs an operator or agent N round trips equal to its missing-field count.

A dangling relative link inside a skill is never reported, because frontmatter validation short-circuits before any reference check. A probe SKILL.md citing references/missing-file.md passed through three validator runs (each failing on a different missing frontmatter field) without the nonexistent path ever being mentioned, so skill-level link rot of the same class already found in sk-doc itself is invisible to the validator sk-doc ships.

The v4.0.1.0 Clearer Skill Docs claim that a skill with no ROUTER.md now fails package_skill.py --strict cannot be observed from a fresh skill: frontmatter validation runs before routing-shape validation, so a probe with no ROUTER.md fails first on an undocumented allowed-tools requirement, and --strict and --check return an identical first error with identical exit 1. The headline routing-shape guarantee is unreachable behind the frontmatter gate.

validate_document.py resolves relative links only inside code-folder READMEs and skips every target not beginning with ./ or ../, so a document citing references/does-not-exist.md in bare form produces only the missing-overview blocking error and the document_type_fallback warning and never mentions the dangling link. Bare-hub-relative citation is exactly how hub docs name their sibling files, which is the mechanical reason sk-doc's own link rot survived its own validator.

Both validators report honest exit codes in both directions (broken skill 1, broken doc 1, healthy sk-prompt SKILL.md 0 with Total issues: 0), and the document_type_fallback warning is a strong operator message because it names both the cause and the remedy by suggesting --type. An earlier apparent exit-0-on-failure was a measurement artifact of capturing tail's status through a pipe, not a validator defect.
Every file a hub ships under references/ or assets/ is reachable from at least one artifact an agent loads, counting leaf-manifest membership and convention-picked siblings as reachability.
A release note claim about what a validator rejects must be reproducible from a fresh, minimal input; if an earlier gate masks the claimed check, the claim is unobservable and counts as drift.
